region: Ovid · Cayuga Lake, Finger Lakes, New York
about: Six Eighty Cellars is a young winery on the steep west bank of Cayuga Lake, near Ovid. Dave and Melissa Pittard, owners of neighbouring Buttonwood Grove Winery, bought the former Toro Run Winery and its mature vineyards in 2020 and opened Six Eighty in 2021, naming it for the 680-foot rise from the lake floor to the top of the property. Head winemaker Ian Barry has made the winery a place for experiment, with clay, terracotta, sandstone and concrete vessels and grapes rarely seen in the region.

Chenin Blanc, the great white grape of France’s Loire Valley, is one of those rarities in the Finger Lakes. Its naturally high acidity suits the region’s cool climate, and it can be made in styles from bone dry to sweet. Six Eighty’s 2024 is a dry, medium-bodied version from the Cayuga Lake side of the region, at 12.7% alcohol. The winery’s note finds honeysuckle, lemon and honeydew on the nose, then a bright, mouth-watering palate of pear skin and lime, finishing soft and round.

This is a brisk, textural Chenin with a quiet power: nectarine, citrus oil, lemon blossom and slate and a long, generous finish, adding that it can be enjoyed now or cellared. That pairing of fresh acidity with quiet weight is what Chenin Blanc is prized for in the Loire, and why it is a grape worth watching in the Finger Lakes.
